external_entities.name: Shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API.

external_entities.name: Card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party card processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: Storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: Order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders and reads and writes order data.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: Receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing completed-order receipts.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Shopper sign-in to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper submission of orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: process order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service for order processing.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read/write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes order data in orders-db.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes completed-order receipts to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.data_description: Receipt records identifying the written order and the order service

data_flows.name: payment webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to notify the storefront API that an order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: Core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network where the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: Card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party environment controlling the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The Storefront API presents a web interface.
assumptions.basis: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API; an API used as a storefront interface is treated as web.

assumptions.assumption: The Order service presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The service is described as a gRPC endpoint; gRPC is a non-web RPC interface.
The database contains shopper addresses and card-last-four data, which are personal and payment data.

assumptions.assumption: The Receipt archive contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: The bucket contains completed-order receipts, which are payment-related business records.
